Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, with Md. Asaduzzaman, Mahbubey Alam and Khondker Mohsenuddin Ahmed, Advocates -------- For the Petitioner. 
Moksudor Rahman, with SAM Mahboob Elahi, Advocates -------- For the Respondent Nos. 1 and 2. 
MA Mannan Talukder, Advocate -------- For the Respondent No. 3.
parties:
Kazi Shafiul Nasher  -------- Petitioner.
Vs.
Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board, Jessore and others  -------- Respondents.
full_judgment:
2. The case of the petitioner, Kazi Shafiul Nasher, is that he appeared in the SSC Examination from St. Joseph's High School, Khulna in 1988 conducted by the respondent No. 1-Board and came out successful standing first in order of merit in the said Board. Thereafter, he got himself admitted as a student of 1st, year HSC (Science) in Dhaka College and had been prosecuting his studies and filled up forms to sit for the HSC Examination from Dhaka College, Dhaka. Before the SSC Examination the father of the petitioner Kazi Lokman Hossain was transferred to Babuganj Upazila as Upazila Nirbahi Officer and as such he got his examination centre transferred from Khulna to Babuganj centre. Before the SSC Examination result was published, an Inquiry Committee was formed consisting of three members, namely, Mr. Taheruddin, Principal, Jessore Women's College, Mr. Tayebur Rahman, Inspector of Schools, Jessore Board and Mr. Narayan Chandra Biswas, Additional District Magistrate, Bakerganj to enquire into the alleged unfair means adopted by the petitioner. The said Inquiry Committee held enquiry, examined witnesses and also examined relevant papers and submitted a report after visiting the examination centre opining that the petitioner sat for the examination properly and nothing was found against the petitioner. The disciplinary committee of the said Board accepted the said report and thereafter the result of the petitioner was published on 14.7.88 showing him standing first in order of merit in the said Board. While the petitioner had been prosecuting his studies in the Dhaka College as aforesaid he was served with a notice dated 28.10.89 (Annexure B) issued by the Controller of Examinations, the respondent No.2, calling upon him to show cause why the result of his SSC Examination should not be cancelled and he should not be suitably punished on the charge of violating the examination rules. The petitioner showed cause by letter dated 3.11.89 (Annexure C). During the period of examination there was no allegation or complaint by the Invigilator or anyone and there was no occasion to take any step under the disciplinary rules and the petitioner was never suspected to have adopted unfair means. Thereafter, the petitioner was informed by a memo dated 13.5.90 that the result of his SSC Examination was cancelled and he was debarred from sitting for the SSC Examination for the years 1989 and 1990. It is the further case of the petitioner that he was never asked to appear before any Inquiry Committee and he was not shown any document and the names of the witnesses were not disclosed to him nor even the names of the members of the Inquiry Committee. The petitioner was not given any opportunity to see what was the evidence recorded against him and he was not allowed either to cross examine or to confront the witnesses to prove his innocence. The regulation under which the action was taken has no application to the petitioner's case and that the petitioner having not been given any opportunity to cross examine the witnesses, the decision of the respondents is arbitrary and without lawful authority. It was also the case of the petitioner that after the result was published-declared and certificate was granted, the petitioner cannot be deprived of his right to hold the certificate after publication of the result in the Gazette and this right cannot be taken away by the respondents and that the whole enquiry was held behind his back and the action of the respondents is malafide and it was taken for collateral purpose at the instance of the enemies of the petitioner's father. It is also the case of the petitioner that one Mr. Md. Atiar Rahman, Professor of MM College, Jessore was behind the matter. 

 4. The respondent No. 2, the Controller of Examinations, Board of Intermediate & Secondary Education, Jessore filed an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the material allegations made in the writ petition and contending, in substance, that an Inquiry Committee was formed to investigate into the allegations received by the Board to the effect that the petitioner adopted unfair means in the SSC Examination, 1988 consisting of three members but the said report did not adequately cover the allegations made by the Head Examiner concerned and the said report was accepted on good faith and the result of the petitioner was also published, as the result of all the four Education Boards to be published on the same day and there was no time to further scrutinize the matter. However, it was published on condition that the Board reserved the authority to change, correct or cancel the publication. One Abdur Rahman of Tootpara, Khulna on behalf of the citizens of Khulna city sent a representation to the then president of Bangladesh challenging the correctness of the said first inquiry report and prayed for further enquiry with copies to the secretary of the respondent No. 1 Board and others including the Secretary, Ministry of Education. The Chairman, Jessore Education Board received a copy of the same from the Ministry of Education requiring the Board to make further enquiry into the matter. Thereafter, by order of the Chairman of the said Board, a Second Inquiry Committee was formed consisting of four distinguished educationists and the said committee issued a notice to the petitioner asking him to appear before the said second inquiry committee for interrogation on 9.8.89 at Babuganj Pilot High School. The petitioner accordingly appeared before the committee and he was interrogated and he gave replies to the questions asked, in writing in his own hand. The said inquiry committee visited various places and examined good number of witnesses and thereafter submitted a report to the Chairman of the respondent No.1 Board on 25.10.89 fmding that the answer script of Science II paper submitted in the name of the petitioner was not written by him at the examination hall within the scheduled time, Mr. Nur Mohammad, the secretary of the Examination Centre (Respondent No. 3) kept 20 blank original answer scripts and some additional blank answer scripts at the residence of the petitioner's father who was the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Babuganj and was the president of the Centre Committee and Supervisory Officer of the Examination Centre where the petitioner sat for examination and that the answer scripts were written by using some of the those blank scripts kept at the residence of the petitioner's father. He misused his official power by giving undue advantage to his son to adopt unfair means in the examination and the said advantage was availed of by the petitioner and he adopted unfair means in the examination. The petitioner filled up his application form to sit for the SSC Examination, 1988 from the SI. Joseph's High School, Khulna and at that time all the members of the petitioner's family except his father were residing at their own house of Khulna and the petitioner had no necessity of changing the examination centre from Khulna but suppressing the said fact the order of transfer was procured from Khulna to Babuganj by misrepresentation of fact. The said Inquiry Committee submitted its report on 24.10.89 recommending, amongst others, (a) cancellation of the result of the petitioner's SSC examination for the year 1988 and debarring him from appearing in the SSC Examination to be held in 1989, (b) to take legal action against the petitioner's father (c) to take appropriate action to remove Mr. Nur Mohammad, the Headmaster of Babuganj Pilot High School (Respondent No.3) and Mr. Md. Ishaque, Senior Teacher of the said school from service, The allegations brought against the petitioner are based on findings arrived at by the Inquiry Committee which submitted the report after making thorough enquiry and considering the replies given by the petitioner. It was further stated that the petitioner's father was transferred to Babuganj not from Khulna but from Satkhira and he served in different stations for about 10 years before his transfer to Babuganj keeping his family althrough at Khulna. Mr. Nur Mohammad (Respondent No.2) admitted in writing in his own hand before the Inquiry Committee that he had to keep 20 blank original answer scripts at the residence of the petitioner's father who was the President of the Centre Committee Babuganj and Supervisory. Officer of the Examination Centre and the answer scripts submitted by the petitioner were written using some of those blank papers kept in his father's custody. The said Mr. Nur Mohammad also stated before the Inquiry Committee that 6n months after the examination was over the petitioner's father left 14 additional blank answer scripts with one Mr. Mcaer Ahmed, Upazila Accounts Officer, Babuganj at the time of his transfer and Mr. Nur Mohammad received these scripts from Mr. Meser Ali giving written receipt. It is also stated that two departmental proceedings are now pending against the petitioner's father for misusing of official power and helping the petitioner in adopting unfair means in the said examination. Before the Inquiry Committee the petitioner was asked to reply to some questions in writing in his own hand. In Science-II paper signature of one Md. Ishaque was appearing who was neither an invigilator nor an authority of the examination centre. A proceeding is pending against said Nur Mohammad and Md. Ishaque for helping the petitioner in adopting unfair means. The written scripts in the name of the petitioner were not written in the examination hall and said Mr. Md. Ishaque and Mr. Nur Mohammad were in collusion with the petitioner's father. The reply of the petitioner was considered by the committee constituted by the Board and it was found that the said reply did not exonerate the petitioner from the allegations. The report of the Inquiry Committee, the show cause notice issued to the petitioner and the petitioner's reply along with papers and documents were placed before the Disciplinary Committee of the Board which in its meeting examined all papers and took an unanimous decision recommending the punishment. Thereafter the matter was placed before the Examination Committee which considered the recommendation of the Disciplinary Committee and endorsed the same and thereafter the matter was placed before the Board which inflicted the punishment in question on the petitioner. It has further been stated in the affidavit- in-opposition that the members of the inquiry committee visited Babuganj wherefrom the petitioner appeared and they were introduced to him. The petitioner was examined personally and questions were put to him by the committee and the petitioner gave answer in writing. The committee showed the available scripts deposited by the petitioner and he was asked to re-write the script of Science-II Paper and was informed of the names of the witnesses. After receipt of the inquiry report the petitioner was asked to show cause against the allegations framed against him on the basis of the inquiry report (Annexure B) to the affidavits-in-opposition and he also replied to the same (Annexure C). The Inquiry Committee recorded the deposition of the witnesses in presence of the petitioner at Babuganj Pilot High School. 

 6. Khondker Mahabubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that although the Board has authority to cancel the certificate but as there is no regulation for that purpose the proceeding itself is void and that the Board has no authority to cancel the result which had already been published. He further submits that there is provision for taking action for adopting unfair means before the result is published where the candidate is suspected to have adopted unfair means and if reported by the invigilator or Officer-in-Charge of the centre and that as there was no report against the petitioner during continuance of the examination, no action can be taken against him. He further submits that as an inquiry was held before publication of the result and the said Inquiry Committee found him not guilty and the authority having accepted that report and published the result, it has no authority to take further action in the matter after the result was officially published. He has drawn our attention to Regulation 157 of the connected regulations. He has also drawn our attention to section 18(2) (VIII) of the Intermediate & Secondary Education Ordinance, 1961 and also section 39 (2)(III) of the said Ordinance. He further submits under section 39(2)(III) the Board has given power to frame regulations providing for gaining and 'withholding' certificate but there is no provision for making regulation for 'withdrawal' of certificate and as such after the result is finally published the Board has no authority to cancel the result of the examination and to withdraw the certificate or to award any other punishment in this connection. He further submits that in any view of the matter the petitioner having not been given the opportunity to cross-examine the witness, on the basis of whose deposition the punishment was awarded, the principle of natural justice was violated and on that ground also the punishment is unauthorised. 

 So, it appears from section 39 (1) that the Board has power to make any regulation for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of the Ordinance generally though some particular subjects are enumerated in 39(2) which are not exhaustive, Moreover, section 39(2) empowers the Board to frame regulation for granting and withholding of certificate. Withholding of certificate is obviously for a temporary period and ultimately either it will be granted or withdrawn. So, it cannot be said that. the Board has no authority to withdraw certificate. Hence, although no regulation for withdrawal of certificate in particular has been framed, the Board is not powerless if any unfair means is found to have been adopted and it is detected after the result is published and the certificate is granted as the law has given it power to do so. In the regulations framed some procedures are there for dealing with the situation arising out of reported unfair means in the examination hall. Regulation 157 contains Discipline Rules in case of suspected commission of unfair means. It is mentioned in paragraph 2 of Regulation 157 (d) "Any case not falling within the above rules shall be decided by the Board in accordance with the nature of the offence on the recommendation of the Discipline Committee". 

 11. The petitioner appeared in the SSC Examination held in March, 1988. On the basis of some allegations an inquiry was held and the report of the inquiry was submitted on 7.7.88. The result of the examination was published on 14.7.88. The petitioner stood first therein. It appears that on 15.7.88 one Abdur Rahman made a complaint to the President of Bangladesh by name (Annexure X to the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent No.2) stating to be an inhabitant of Khulna Town endorsing copies to others namely, Minister-in- Charge of the Ministry of Education and Establishment, Government of Bangladesh, Secretary and Controller of Examinations, Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Jessore, making certain allegation about unfair means to have been adopted by the petitioner taking advantages of his father's position. Therefore the instant inquiry was held. 

 17. So it appears that the impugned order was passed by the respondent Board in accordance with law after compliance with the requirements of the principle of natural justice and after getting the matter inquired into by an Inquiry Committee which submitted the reports after hearing the petitioner in person and considering his explanation and after giving the petitioner another opportunity to show cause considering his reply thereto. Besides the Inquiry Committee, the matter was considered by the Discipline Committee, the Examination Committee and finally by the Board.
